chunks: Multiple narrators from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Basri from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi from Harun ibn Kharja from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you intend a matter, take six pieces of paper and write in three of them: 'In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Goodness is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, for so-and-so son of so-and-so: Do it'; and in the other three: 'In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Goodness is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, for so-and-so son of so-and-so: Do not do it'.

Then place them beneath your prayer mat, then pray two Rak'at. When you are finished, prostrate and say one hundred times: 'I seek Allah's choice by His mercy, a choice in well-being.' Then sit upright and say: 'O Allah, choose for me and select for me in all my affairs, in ease from You and well-being.'

Then strike with your hand to the papers, mix them, and draw one. If three 'Do it' come out consecutively, do the matter you intended; and if three 'Do not do' come out consecutively, do not do it; and if one 'Do it' comes out and the other two are 'Do not do', then draw from the papers up to five, and look at the majority of them and act upon it, and leave the sixth, as you are not in need of it.
ai.seo_question: What is the method and supplication for Istikhara according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the ritual of Istikhara using lots (qur'ah), a method distinct from the supplication-based Istikhara, emphasizing the Imam's guidance in decision-making. It prescribes a structured process of writing options on paper, performing two Rak'at of prayer, and casting lots to reveal divine preference, reflecting the Shia tradition of seeking clarity through both spiritual devotion and tangible signs. The practice underscores the belief that Allah facilitates ease and choice for the believer, aligning human intent with divine wisdom.
